title: Microsoft 365 Messaging Support Operations — ITIL Incident & Problem Management Runbook
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (enterprise Exchange/M365 messaging operations).

Exchange admin center / M365 admin center / Exchange Online PowerShell (EXO V3) / Microsoft Graph and on-prem Exchange Server + AD authored at exact detail from Microsoft public docs; version-/plan-dependent behavior (Exchange Server CU, EOP vs Defender for Office 365 plan, EOA/auto-expanding archive availability, Commercial vs Government cloud) cited or flagged 'verify in your tenant/version', never invented. Third-party hygiene/archiving/gateway tools at the pattern level. Automation is PowerShell (EXO PowerShell / Graph) — no hardcoded credentials or secrets in code. No client names.
hook: Run L2–L4 Microsoft 365 messaging support to SLA with ITIL discipline
problem: A messaging support team lives or dies by consistent operations — SLAs met, escalations clean, root causes fixed, and knowledge captured. This solution is the messaging-specific support-operations runbook: L2/L3/L4 responsibilities and escalation, ITIL incident and problem management for mail issues, on-call, service-availability handling, First-Call-Resolution/CSAT and reopen-reduction practices, and knowledge-base + coaching workflows — so the team delivers to SLA with a positive customer experience. (Scoped to messaging support ops — distinct from a general desktop-support runbook or security incident response.)
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the messaging support operating model: L2–L4 roles + escalation, ITIL incident/problem management for mail, on-call, SLA/FCR/CSAT, and KB/coaching.
Requirements Guide — each prerequisite with how to verify/implement (a ticketing/ITSM tool + SLAs, messaging admin access for the team, on-call rota, KB platform).

Implementation Guide — define L2–L4 responsibilities + escalation paths, stand up incident and problem management for messaging, wire on-call + service-availability handling, set the FCR/CSAT/reopen practices, and operate KB + coaching — each runbook named.

5 PowerShell scripts — Discovery, Configuration/Remediation, Validation, Reporting, and a scope/health helper — authentic Exchange Online PowerShell (EXO V3) / Microsoft Graph automation (read-only or -WhatIf by default; no credentials in code).
Runbook Library + validation gates (SLAs tracked, problems closed with root cause, KB current) plus Best Practices for a high-CSAT messaging support practice.
short: A messaging-specific support-operations runbook — L2–L4 roles + escalation, ITIL incident & problem management for mail, on-call, SLA/FCR/CSAT practices, and KB/coaching — so the team delivers to SLA with a positive customer experience. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
